newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 15.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 15.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
LONDON - All European Union states should ban tobacco advertising and move to limit smoking in any way they can, says Europe's social affairs commissioner Padraig Flynn.
FRANKFURT - The main association of German advertising agencies, GWA, says most of its members are satisfied with business in the first half of the year and predict further growth in the second half.

IRVING, Texas - Evergreen Media Corp and Chancellor Broadcasting Co say they have a definitive agreement to acquire Katz Media Group Inc for about $373 million. Katz sells national advertising time for radio stations, television stations, cable systems and Internet sites throughout the U.S.

LONDON - Virgin Group boss Richard Branson says his companies will sponsor sports that lose any funding from tobacco companies. "Even an international sport like the Grand Prix need not suffer," he says.
NEW YORK - BNN Corp forms a unit with Interpublic Group of Cos Inc to handle sports and event marketing for General Motors Corp.
LONDON - Some 61 percent of Britons back a complete ban on tobacco advertising, an idea currently being considered by the government, according to a survey by the Office of National Statistics.
GREENWICH, Connecticut - NFO Research Inc. agrees to buy market research firm MBL Group Plc in a deal valued at $55 million.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
HAMBURG - Italian fashion group Benetton is looking for a German publisher for its in-house-produced magazine Colors, marketing newsletter New Business reports.

LONDON - Business and industry magazine publisher Euromoney Publications Plc is expected to announce shortly that it is buying Institutional Investor from Walt Disney, the Guardian newspaper says. Euromoney is expected to pay up to $130 million for the specialist financial publications house.
CANBERRA - The Australian government says it will develop a national voluntary code aimed at regulating the content of on-line services, without restricting industry growth.

HAMBURG - The German weekly news magazine Der Spiegel and Deutsche Bahn railway company have started a daily newspaper for German rail travellers aimed at business readers on late-afternoon express trains.
NEW YORK - Time Warner Inc Chief Financial Officer Richard Bressler says the company doesn't expect to make any more significant acquisitions in the foreseeable future.
LOS ANGELES - The WB Television Network, owned by Time Warner Inc, says five stations affiliated with rival United Paramount Network have agreed to switch to The WB in January 1998.

FRANKFURT - A week after their much-hyped launch following a frantic subscription period, shares in television network ProSieben Media AG have settled at a solid but modest premium to their issue price.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BRUSSELS - West European car sales soared nine percent year-on-year in June, partly reflecting a booming Italian market triggered by an incentive scheme, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association says.

TOKYO - Canon Inc says it has developed the world's first chip for digital video cameras. The new chip paves the way for the development of smaller, energy-saving, higher quality cameras which can be easily connected to personal computers and other multimedia equipment, Canon says.

SEOUL - Two years after South Korea agreed to take additional steps to open up its auto market, the country remains "very, very closed" to imports, the president of the American Automobile Manufacturers' Association says.

UDINE, Italy - An Italian company says it will not take its "Fuehrer" wine off the market despite a storm of protest. The wine, which shows Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler on the label, comes in two types -- "Sieg Heil" (Hail Victory) and "Ein Volk, Ein Reich, Ein Fuehrer" (One People, One Empire, One Leader). It also sells other wines named after Che Guevara, Lenin and Karl Marx.
TOKYO - Inchcape Peugeot Japan Co Ltd, the Japanese import and distribution unit for Peugeot cars, says it is aiming for Japanese sales of 20,000 cars in the year 2000.
BEIJING - A corporate restructuring by China's Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd is aimed at rebuilding the beer maker's image and will boost returns for investors, the China Daily says.
TOKYO - Sales of Bandai Co Ltd's "virtual pet" Tamagotchi are expected to reach 10 million, the business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reports.
BEIJING - China is to set up several large-scale chain store groups in the next five to 10 years in a bid to make its domestic retail sector more competitive, the People's Daily says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
KUALA LUMPUR- From the price of wheat to petrol, Southeast Asian consumers may begin feeling the pinch of rising interest rates, analysts say.

JERUSALEM - The sign outside the door reads "Coffee Shop," but visitors at the cafe just inside Jerusalem's walled Old City get more than a cappuccino. Known in Christian circles as a cafe on the "cutting edge of modern-day evangelism," and to Jews and Moslems as a place to avoid, the Loaves & Fishes Cafe employs young missionaries zealous about spreading the word.
HO CHI MINH CITY, Vietnam - Vietnamese architects have a solution for the city's overcrowding -- build satellite cities and move some 600,000 people into them.
ANGKOR WAT, Cambodia - A bloody coup and the onset of the rainy season have left Cambodia's magnificent 12th century ruins at Angkor Wat high and dry for tourists, say tourism officials.
